newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Gazprom plans Black Sea gas pipeline to Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom plans Black Sea gas pipeline to Turkey.

text.p: Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom said on Tuesday that it plans to build a gas pipeline under the Black Sea to export supplies to Turkey, but declined to say whether it would issue paper to finance it.

A company statement said that Petergaz, a joint venture between Gazprom and private Dutch company Heerema, would oversee the proposal, one of Gazprom's five large projects to increase Russian natural gas exports to Europe and the Mediterranean.
Gazprom, the world's largest natural gas producer, is selling American Depositary Shares to help finance its $40 billion Yamal-Europe gas pipeline, its biggest pipeline project.

Gazprom spokesman Vladimir Zhukov said he had no details on costs or time frames for the Turkish project, which envisions construction of a pipeline from Izobilnoye, 100 km east of Krasnodar in southern Russia, to the Black Sea outlet Tuapse and under the Black Sea to eastern Turkey.
The pipeline would rest in some places more than 2,000 meters below sea level.

"The realisation of the Turkish project will allow us to resolve not only the energy problems of the eastern, central and Mediterranean regions of Turkey, but will also attract indispensable investments for tapping new reserves, developing existing reserves and for reconstructing the Russian network," the release said.

Turkey said in August it planned to finalise a $1.1 billion deal with Russia to build a 1,160 km (720 mile) pipeline from Russia to Turkey with a capacity of up to 16 billion cubic metres (bcm) of gas a year.
It did not specify the route then.
Gazprom has said it hopes to boost gas exports to Turkey to 30 bcm a year from six bcm.
